nary_nodes.label: Benoît Castel crowned World Confectioner
evidence: the International Union of Bakers and Confectioners (UIBC) named him World Confectioner of the Year last month.
Castel received the UIBC award presented annually to a leading figure in the profession in recognition of their career and contribution to the trade on July 14 in Singapore.

nary_nodes.label: Castel's mission to be world champion
evidence: "I have a mission: to be the world champion every day in my shop for my customers," he said, eyes twinkling.

nary_nodes.label: Nina Métayer crowned champion
evidence: Three years after fellow French pastry chef Nina Métayer was crowned champion, Castel received the UIBC award presented annually to a leading figure in the profession in recognition of their career and contribution to the trade on July 14 in Singapore.

nary_nodes.label: Castel's motto: "It's all about the product."
evidence: At the helm of several establishments in Paris, Castel has never strayed from his motto: "It's all about the product."

nary_nodes.label: Castel on importance of work
evidence: "Our work is no trivial matter, every day we make things that people put into their bodies," said Castel, who hails from Brittany in western France.

nary_nodes.label: Castel on stopping chocolate choux pastry
evidence: "If we stopped making it, there'd be protests," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Grandparents making butter
evidence: The grandson of farmers, he grew up watching his grandparents make their own butter.

nary_nodes.label: Castel on mother and grandmother's cooking
evidence: "My mother and my grandmother cook divinely well," he said.

nary_nodes.label: Castel wanted to become a chef
evidence: From the age of seven, he wanted to become a chef and received his first recipe book.

nary_nodes.label: Castel received first recipe book
evidence: From the age of seven, he wanted to become a chef and received his first recipe book.

nary_nodes.label: Pastry chef spinning sugar model
evidence: But it was watching a pastry chef spin a model of the famed Loire valley Château de Chambord out of sugar while out to dinner three years later that set him firmly on the path of pastry-making.

nary_nodes.label: Castel on product dictating recipe
evidence: "The funny thing with this profession is that it's the product that dictates the recipe," he said enthusiastically from his kitchen, which opens onto the shop and the dining room, a popular spot for brunch.

nary_nodes.label: Romain Montbabut working with Castel
evidence: Dressed in his white pastry chef's jacket embroidered with his name, he works with Romain Montbabut, his head baker, with whom he regularly tests new recipes.
Montbabut, who has been working with him for six years.

nary_nodes.label: Montbabut's description of Castel
evidence: The pastry chef is "demanding, he has this slightly perfectionist side we're very fond of", said Montbabut, who has been working with him for six years.
"He's there alongside his workers every day and loves to pass things on," he added.

nary_nodes.label: Castel and Margot opening new venue

evidence: "These days, I'm as much a cook, a gardener and a baker as I am a pastry chef," he said.
